questions.q: What specific problem does a self-service infrastructure template remove, according to this lesson?
options: The human relay in the middle -- filing a ticket and waiting for an engineer to manually run Terraform -- not Terraform itself
The need to use Terraform at all for provisioning databases or queues
The need for any version control on infrastructure code
The requirement that infrastructure ever be reviewed by anyone
questions.explain: Terraform still does the same plan and apply work. What changes is who triggers it and how fast: a developer's form submission instead of a ticket sitting in a backlog waiting for a human to run it by hand.

questions.q: In the provision-postgres-db template, what does the terraform:run step actually do?
options: It lets the developer write and submit arbitrary Terraform code for review
It runs the same Terraform module the platform team already wrote and vetted, using the developer's form inputs as variables
It only validates the form without provisioning anything
It replaces Terraform with a different provisioning engine specific to Backstage
questions.explain: The template runs a fixed, already-reviewed module with the submitted parameters as input -- the developer never writes or chooses the underlying Terraform.

questions.q: Why does restricting sizeTier to an enum of three values matter more for safety than having a human approve every request?
options: It doesn't actually improve safety; enums are purely a UI convenience
Enums make the form load faster but have no effect on what can be provisioned

A human approver reading every request is just a ticket queue with a form in front of it; a bounded, vetted enum structurally prevents a developer from requesting a configuration that was never approved
It only matters in the dev environment, never in staging or prod
questions.explain: Bounding the parameter to pre-approved values enforces the constraint at the form level, which scales, instead of relying on a person to catch bad requests one at a time.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how should a request for environment: prod be handled without recreating a general ticket queue?
options: It should be blocked entirely, since self-service templates can never target production
It should require the same multi-day review as every other request
It should be left completely unchecked, since the module is already vetted
With a scoped, automated policy check or a single specific reviewer notified for that one request, rather than a general backlog every request passes through
questions.explain: A narrow, automated or lightly-scoped gate on the genuinely risky case preserves safety without turning every routine request back into a queue.

questions.q: Why does the template's final register-resource step matter for a database it just provisioned?
options: It registers the database as a Resource entity linked via dependsOn to the requesting Component, so later questions like 'what uses this database' have a real answer
It deletes the database if the request is later found invalid
It encrypts the database credentials inside the catalog
It is only used for billing purposes and has no catalog effect
questions.explain: Without that registration, the database exists in the cloud provider's console but is effectively invisible to the catalog -- exactly the discoverability gap Lesson 5 described for unregistered services.
